blocks.title: Friday afternoon at work in Ottawa
blocks.context: Mei and Olivier talk about their plans before the weekend.

lines.speaker: Olivier
lines.fr: Alors, Mei, qu'est-ce que tu vas faire ce week-end ?
lines.en: So, Mei, what are you going to do this weekend?

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.fr: Samedi, je vais faire du ski avec mes enfants. Il va faire beau !
lines.en: On Saturday, I'm going to go skiing with my kids. The weather's going to be nice!

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.fr: Dimanche, je vais rester à la maison. Je vais faire le ménage, et après, je vais me reposer. Et toi ?
lines.en: On Sunday, I'm going to stay home. I'm going to clean the house, and after that I'm going to rest. And you?

lines.speaker: Olivier
lines.fr: Moi, je vais aller à Montréal. Mon frère va fêter ses quarante ans.
lines.en: I'm going to go to Montréal. My brother is going to celebrate his fortieth birthday.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.fr: Ah, c'est bien ! Tu vas prendre le train ?
lines.en: Oh, that's nice! Are you going to take the train?

lines.speaker: Olivier
lines.fr: Non, nous allons prendre la voiture. Et la semaine prochaine, je vais commencer un nouveau travail !
lines.en: No, we're going to take the car. And next week, I'm going to start a new job!

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.fr: C'est vrai ? Félicitations ! Tu vas travailler où ?
lines.en: Really? Congratulations! Where are you going to work?

lines.speaker: Olivier
lines.fr: À Gatineau, dans une école. Mais je ne vais pas changer d'appartement : je vais rester à Ottawa.
lines.en: In Gatineau, in a school. But I'm not going to change apartments: I'm going to stay in Ottawa.

blocks.body: Listen for [[vais]], [[va]], [[allons]] followed by a second verb. Each one is a plan.

blocks.title: Aller + infinitive = going to
blocks.body:
You already know [[aller]] (to go). Put an **infinitive** after it and you get the near future, exactly like English “going to”: [[Je vais travailler.]] = I'm going to work.

French speakers use it all the time for plans and for things that are about to happen. In conversation it is far more common than the “real” future tense, so you can already talk about the future with one verb you know.

blocks.title: Aller + travailler
head: aller + infinitive
English
rows: he / she is going to work (on: we're going to work)
you're going to work (formal or plural)
blocks.note: Only [[aller]] changes. The second verb stays in the infinitive. You can even say [[je vais aller]] (I'm going to go).

blocks.title: Saying when
blocks.note:
Put the time marker at the **start** or at the **end**: [[Ce soir, je vais cuisiner.]] = [[Je vais cuisiner ce soir.]]

Useful markers: [[ce soir]], [[demain]], [[demain matin]], [[ce week-end]], [[la semaine prochaine]], [[le mois prochain]], [[l'année prochaine]], [[bientôt]].

examples.fr: Demain matin, je vais faire du sport.
examples.en: Tomorrow morning, I'm going to exercise.

examples.fr: Nous allons visiter Vancouver l'année prochaine.
examples.en: We're going to visit Vancouver next year.
It's going to snow this weekend.

examples.fr: Tu vas te coucher tôt ce soir ?
examples.en: Are you going to go to bed early tonight?

blocks.title: Negatives and questions
blocks.body:
**Negative:** [[ne… pas]] goes around the form of *aller*: [[Je ne vais pas travailler.]] [[Nous n'allons pas sortir.]] (We're not going to go out. *ne* → *n'* before a vowel.)

**Questions**, in three registers, as in lesson 1:

- [[Tu vas faire quoi ce soir ?]] (informal)
- [[Qu'est-ce que tu vas faire ce soir ?]] (neutral)
- [[Que vas-tu faire ce soir ?]] (formal)

**Reflexive verbs:** the little pronoun matches the subject and sits right before the infinitive: [[je vais me reposer]], [[tu vas te reposer]], [[elle va se reposer]].

blocks.title: Words and phrases in this lesson

blocks.body:
- **Infinitive, not a conjugated verb:** [[Je vais travailler]], not *je vais travaille*.
- **No preposition:** not *je vais à travailler*.
- **Negation around aller:** [[Je ne vais pas manger]], not *je vais ne pas manger*.
- **ils vont, not ils font:** [[Ils vont jouer]] (they're going to play) ≠ [[Ils font du sport]] (they do sports).
- **Prochain agrees:** [[le mois prochain]], but [[la semaine prochaine]] and [[l'année prochaine]] (feminine).
- **demain matin**, with no article: not *demain le matin*.

blocks.title: The weather forecast
blocks.body: Weather forecasts use the near future all the time. Combine it with the weather phrases you know:

examples.en: Tomorrow it's going to be cold.

examples.fr: Ce week-end, il va faire beau et chaud.
examples.en: This weekend it's going to be nice and warm.

blocks.body:
- In Québec, **the weekend** is usually [[la fin de semaine]]: [[Qu'est-ce que tu vas faire en fin de semaine ?]] and on Friday everyone says [[Bonne fin de semaine !]]
- [[Tantôt]] in Québec means **a little later today** (or a little earlier today, depending on the verb tense): [[Je vais faire le ménage tantôt.]] = I'm going to clean later.
- In relaxed Québec speech you'll hear [[à soir]] for *ce soir*: [[On va au cinéma à soir ?]] Recognize it, but write [[ce soir]].

examples.en: I'm going to do the grocery shopping later today. (Québec)

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: Ce soir, je vais cuisiner et je vais regarder un film. Ce week-end, je ne vais pas travailler : je vais faire du vélo avec ma fille. La semaine prochaine, je vais commencer un cours de français. Et l'année prochaine, nous allons visiter Québec. Et toi, qu'est-ce que tu vas faire ce week-end ?
models.en: Tonight I'm going to cook and watch a movie. This weekend I'm not going to work: I'm going to go cycling with my daughter. Next week I'm going to start a French class. And next year we're going to visit Québec City. And you, what are you going to do this weekend?

blocks.prompt: Write a message to a friend about your plans for the weekend: two things you're going to do, one thing you're not going to do, and a question about their plans.

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: Salut Amira ! Samedi matin, je vais faire le ménage. Samedi soir, je vais manger au restaurant avec mon mari. Dimanche, je ne vais pas sortir : je vais me reposer ! Et toi, tu vas faire quoi en fin de semaine ?
models.en: Hi Amira! On Saturday morning I'm going to clean the house. On Saturday evening I'm going to eat at a restaurant with my husband. On Sunday I'm not going to go out: I'm going to rest! And you, what are you going to do this weekend?

summary:
- Talk about plans with [[aller + infinitif]]: [[je vais travailler, nous allons visiter Québec]]
- Say when: [[ce soir, demain, ce week-end, la semaine prochaine, l'année prochaine]]
- Say what you're not going to do: [[Je ne vais pas travailler.]] and ask [[Qu'est-ce que tu vas faire ?]]
